newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks stage rebound, end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks stage rebound, end sharply higher.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks staged a sharp rebound on Monday, with property stocks in particular notching up strong gains following recent market weakness.
The Hang Seng Index surged 259.84 points, or 2.08 percent, to 12,749.14. Turnover was HK$8.17 billion compared with HK$10.58 billion on Friday.
"The market was extremely oversold over the last two weeks," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
"Most of the property counters have consolidated 15 to 20 percent from their peaks. That is why you see some buying," he said.
Analysts said investors had already discounted a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates at Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve policy-setting meeting.
If the Fed does raise rates it would be a non-event, said Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities.
"Short-term it looks like we can treat this as a technical rebound and there is still some room on the upside," he said.
But Wong noted that Monday's turnover was only moderate and the Hang Seng Index was likely to meet resistance around 12,800 points.
"After such a huge selloff, the magnitude is not that much to be conclusive that we have already seen a reversal of the short-term downtrend," he said.

"I think 12,950 is the pivot point. If it breaks above we can conclude that the correction from 14,000 has possibly ended already and we will see an improvement in sentiment in the medium term," he added.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd jumped HK$3.50 to HK$85.75 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd added HK$3.00 to HK$67.00.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd gained HK$2.25 to HK$70.75 and New World Development Co Ltd advanced HK$1.70 to HK$42.90.
Shares in Hongkong Telecom fell HK$0.45 to HK$13.95 after running up 2.9 percent last week on speculation that a Chinese party would take a stake in the company.
Local media reported on Saturday that China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunication said it would not buy a direct stake in Hongkong Telecom.
HSBC Holdings Plc rose HK$2.00 to HK$178.50 and Hang Seng Bank Ltd gained HK$1.50 to HK$83.25.
March Hang Seng Index futures rose 265 points to 12,715.
